statement: n children stand in a line, and child i has rating ratings[i]. You are handing out candies under two rules: every child gets at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than a neighbour must get more candies than that neighbour.
Return the smallest total number of candies that satisfies both rules.

Do it in two passes. Left to right, give each child one more than the left neighbour when their rating is higher, and 1 otherwise. Right to left, raise a child to one more than the right neighbour when their rating is higher. Each child keeps the larger of the two requirements. Equal ratings impose no rule in either direction.

examples.explanation: The candies come out as [2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1]. The two children rated 2 stand next to each other, so the second needs no more than the first and can have 1. The total is 9.
Giving [1, 2, 1] works: the middle child out-rates the first and gets more, and the last child ties the middle one, so 1 is enough. The total is 4.
